summary: Sustained increase in 5xx errors and streaming disconnects after priority rebalance; upstream runtime CPU saturation and intermittent DNS resolution delays
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-10 16:12 UTC we observed a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the public API for a single dedicated tenant (InklingAI) coinciding with an automated priority reweight roll (infra policy). Impact: customer streaming sessions disconnect frequently and non-streaming generation requests return 502/503 ~10-30% of the time. Business impact: InklingAI reports production user-facing errors and increased latency on inference calls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use InklingAI tenant credentials against prod-us-east endpoint. 2) Send a mix of streaming chat and non-streaming completion requests targeting redwood/open-7B-v0 and redwood/quant-llama-13b. 3) Observe error rate rising after sending sustained concurrent sessions (>=40 concurrent streaming sessions) and during tenant priority rebalance window.
observed_behavior: Intermittent 502 and 503 from API gateway; streaming connections drop with FIN/RST from upstream proxy. Upstream runtimes report CPU exhaustion and frequent GC spikes; occasional DNS resolution failures (socket timeout) when resolving runtime service endpoints.
expected_behavior: Stable <1% 5xx error rate for this tenant during normal concurrency; streaming connections remain established and retries succeed without error amplification.
logs: 2026-03-10T16:14:21Z api-gateway WARN upstream=10.1.8.23:504 502 connection reset by peer
2026-03-10T16:15:05Z runtime[svc-7b-2] ERROR OOM-avoidance: GC pause 120ms CPU 98% slots exhausted
2026-03-10T16:16:48Z dns-client ERROR lookup runtime-prod-host timed out after 250ms
2026-03-10T16:18:03Z api-gateway INFO streaming-session session_id=abc123 terminated: upstream-failure
timeline: 2026-03-10 16:10 UTC - Scheduled infra priority rebalance started (auto roll triggered by policy).
2026-03-10 16:12 UTC - First customer report to support (InklingAI S. Park): "observed elevated errors and dropped streams".
2026-03-10 16:18 UTC - Monitoring alerts: api-gateway 5xx rate for tenant increased from 0.8% to 12%.
2026-03-10 16:25 UTC - SRE paged and began correlation across runtime and DNS subsystems.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation shows timing overlap between priority rebalance (route weight changes) and spike in concurrent connections routed to a subset of runtimes.
Runtime-side telemetry indicates increased CPU utilization concentrated on 3 hosts (svc-7b-2, svc-7b-7, svc-7b-9) with throttling of worker threads and elevated GC activity.
DNS client logs show intermittent 110/ETIMEDOUT errors during bursts; retries sometimes select healthy backends but after delay, amplifying request latency and retries at api-gateway.
Hypothesis A: Priority reweight moved a disproportionate fraction of streaming connections to runtimes with fragmented GPU/CPU schedules, causing local overload and backpressure to api-gateway.
Hypothesis B: DNS resolution delays during rapid route updates caused the proxy to attempt connections to stale addresses, producing resets and cascade retries.
Checked linked dashboards: route-weight change IDs match the rebalance window. No concurrent deploys found in infra deploy log except the automated reweight job.
mitigation: Manually paused the automated priority reweight job at 16:28 UTC (temporary).
Applied route rollback for InklingAI to previous stable weights at 16:30 UTC which shifted traffic away from overloaded runtimes.
Issued a soft client-side retry guidance to InklingAI (increase retry backoff to 300ms) to reduce retry amplification.
Flushed DNS cache on api-gateway proxy instances in the affected AZ to reduce TTL-stale lookups (16:40 UTC).
Scaled up a small pool of additional runtime pods with warmed models (quant-llama-13b) as temporary capacity (16:50 UTC).
SRE placed runtime hosts svc-7b-2 and svc-7b-7 into drain for health checks and monitoring while traffic is rerouted.
resolution_plan: Root cause analysis (next 48h): combine heap/CPU profiles from overloaded hosts with DNS client metrics to confirm causal chain.
Implement safer rebalance algorithm: add per-host load signals and gradual probing to avoid large instant weight shifts (engineering story planned).
Add short-circuit in reweight job to pause when runtime host CPU or GC exceeds threshold (PR created - see infra PR).
Improve DNS client backoff and caching behavior in api-gateway to avoid connection attempts to recently failing addresses.
Follow-up with InklingAI on retry/backoff recommendations and offer dedicated warm capacity plan if expected traffic patterns will remain high.

resolution: Partial mitigation applied: automated priority reweight paused and route rollback executed; DNS caches flushed; temporary capacity added. 5xx rate reduced from ~12% to ~2.3% for the tenant. Investigation ongoing to deliver permanent fixes (see resolution_plan).
follow_up_actions: Create engineering ticket to implement weighted rebalance safety checks and host health gating (ENG-REBAL-2026).
Enhance api-gateway DNS client to avoid tight retry loops and add better logging for resolution latency (ENG-DNS-2026).
Schedule post-incident review with InklingAI, SRE, and infra to review timeline and verify monitoring coverage.
Add synthetic test that simulates rapid reweight to validate system resilience in staging.
